narrative.title: Scheduling Patrols Across a Compound Grid
narrative.scenario: A security grid places n patrol drones so that no two share a column, a row, or any diagonal — one drone per file, and no clear line of sight along a slope. The dispatcher fills the grid one column at a time, trying each row in the current column, and keeps three occupancy ledgers: rows taken, diagonals sloping one way, and diagonals sloping the other. When all n columns hold a drone, the layout is archived.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n, the grid size and drone count.
narrative.outputFormat: Every distinct layout as n row-strings, each 'Q' marking a drone and '.' an empty cell.

complexity.optimalTime: O(n!) upper bound — column-by-column placement with diagonal pruning
complexity.optimalSpace: O(n^2) to store each board plus O(n) recursion depth

testCases.explanation: The 4-grid has exactly two distinct layouts, mirror images of each other.
A single drone is trivially safe.

hintLevels: Level 1: One queen per column removes an entire axis of conflict — only rows and diagonals remain to check.
Level 2: For the current column, test each row against three ledgers: the row, the anti-diagonal indexed by row + col, and the main diagonal by row - col.
Level 3: Offset the row - col index by n to keep it non-negative in an array-backed ledger; set and unset the ledger entry around the recursive call.
